newsitem.title: UK: UK brewers continue to advance on accounting plans.
newsitem.headline: UK brewers continue to advance on accounting plans.

text.p: UK brewing stocks continued to push ahead on Friday after Thursday's Accounting Standards Board (ASB) proposals on the treatment of fixed assets, analysts said.

The impact of the plans for the valuation and depreciation of fixed assets, is likely to be less severe on the industry than many had expected and one analyst said the hit in earnings could be half of what had been feared.
Whitbread added another 10-1/2p to be up 30-1/2p at 728-1/2p since the ASB announcement.
Bass which rose 16-1/2p yesterday was up 10p at 805p.
UBS upgraded its stance on the two stocks yesterday after the ASB discussion paper, said market sources, with Panmure Gordon also reiterating their positive view on the sector.
"The recent underperformance by the brewing sector ran contrary to earnings expectations for 1997," said Panmure Gordon analyst Colin Humphreys.
"The sector had underperformed on an accounting change that turns out not to have been as severe as people feared."
Comments on the ASB discussion paper are due by January 17.
